items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: I remember Mrs. Eggleston she was the boss, she used to come out to the bar and say, Mr. Whaley, would you come and give us some music.

ctx.x: In them days, the average working person was making about that much a week.

Oh, yeah, we were getting $15 a week room and board, see, they roomed us out there. They had a nice bungalow for all the musicians but when we'd get in there, we'd get on the floor at 7 o'clock, start working and we worked till 12 and if people didn't give us any money, we'd go out to the bar and hang out at the bar and I remember Mrs. Eggleston she was the boss, she used to come out to the bar and say, Mr. Whaley, would you come and give us some music.

I said, them people don't want our music. They ain't interested in music. So after awhile I'd go back out and we'd get together and then you'd hear, people would come up or send the waiter up, here's a $5 bill, here's -- play so and so.
